weaknesses: The system records are unhelpful to the rider on the two contact conditions: the driver messaged at 18:22:25 (F10), called at 18:23:25 (F13) and cancelled only at 18:27:55 having been stationary 6 min 0 s at the pickup (F3, F6) — on the face of NS-1 that is a textbook wait-and-cancel, and the rider's own complaint admits he came out late.

There is no record of the scheduled pickup time in the fact table (F4 shows acceptance at 18:19:00 and cancellation at 18:27:55 only), so the rider cannot prove the 8-minute threshold was not reached from the scheduled time rather than from arrival; the platform's recorded arrival at 18:21:55 (F6) is the only start the code can read.

The rider produced no message to the driver between 18:22 and 18:27 (F12 lists only the driver's two messages, both timestamped), so the driver's "No reply from you" (F11) is consistent with the chat record and the rider cannot show he asked the driver to wait.

claims.assertion: The driver cancelled because the rider did not show, not for any reason of his own: his in-app message one minute before cancelling reads "No reply from you, I need to go already, cancelling" (F11), and his written statement reads "After pressing I'm Here I waited more than 5 minutes at the pickup. No rider, so I cancelled" (F14); neither text mentions car trouble, a personal matter, another job or a refusal of the trip, and no cancellation reason was picked in the app (F4).

NS-1(i) is satisfied: the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 18:21:55 only 40 m from the pickup point (F7) and the GPS track independently puts him within 200 m of the pickup from 18:21:40, closest approach 38 m at 18:24:15 (F1, F2), so arrival was recorded with GPS at the pickup point.

NS-1(ii) is satisfied: the 5-minute free wait ran from 18:21:55 (arrival, the later of scheduled pickup and arrival) and the driver cancelled at 18:27:55, i.e. 6 min 0 s after recorded arrival (F6), by which time he had been stationary at the pickup for 6 min 0 s and within 200 m for a cumulative 6 min 15 s (F3, F2).

NS-1(iii) is satisfied: before cancelling the driver sent 2 in-app messages, the first at 18:22:25 (“At the pickup now, grey Kia Niro.”, F10) and the last at 18:27 (“No reply from you, I need to go already, cancelling.”, F11), and made 1 in-app call at 18:23:25 which went unanswered (F5, F13).

NS-1(iv) is satisfied: the driver stayed at the pickup point throughout, stationary 18:21:55–18:27:55 at 40 m from the pickup with no GPS gap, and he cancelled the moment that stationary period ended (F3, F6).

The rider's account that she "came out a minute after the driver cancelled" is contradicted by the system records: the driver was inside 200 m from 18:21:40 and made an in-app call at 18:23:25 and messages at 18:22:25 and 18:27, none of which was answered across a wait of over six minutes before the 18:27:55 cancellation (F2, F5, F13, F4).

The rider's profile shows 0 disputes in 90 days and 0 upheld (F18) and the driver's shows 488 trips in 90 days with 0 upheld disputes in that window (F19), so there is no repeat-violation or fraud basis on either side and no flag_account is warranted here.

weaknesses: The closest approach was 38–40 m, not 0 m, so the rider may argue the driver was never exactly at the pickup point; the 200 m rule is a system default, not an official radius (F1, F3, NS-1).

The driver's 18:27 message “No reply from you, I need to go already, cancelling.” (F11) mixes an unresolved rider with the driver's own convenience ("I need to go already") — the rider can press this as a reason of his own under NS-0/NS-3, though the better reading is that no reply is why he cancelled (F14).

The in-app call at 18:23 was not answered and there is no call recording (F13); if the rider's line shows an incoming call at 18:23 that she missed while on her way out, the wait-vs-reply argument narrows, though the timeline (F5, F6) is unaffected.

The rider's own claim that she came out just one minute after cancellation is a statement only; the judge has no record of her movements, so if the court treats her account as credible it could soften the fee even though every NS-1 condition is met on the system records (NS-1).

points.response: Conceded in its literal reading: the driver's texts (F11) and statement (F14) name no car trouble, personal matter, another job or refusal of the trip, and no app reason was picked (F4), so NS-0:reason reads met — but that only opens NS-1; it does not satisfy NS-1(i)-(iv), which is where this case is decided.

Accepted on the records: NS-1(i) is met — the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 18:21:55, 40 m from the pickup, and the GPS puts him within 200 m from 18:21:40 (F7, F1, F2); the rider does not contest that the driver was at the pickup point.

Accepted: the driver remained within 200 m and stationary at 40 m from the pickup for the whole 6 min 0 s before cancelling, with no GPS gap (F3, F2, F6), so NS-1(iv) is met and there is no ground for flag_account under NS-2.

Accepted: one in-app message at 18:22:25 (F10) and one in-app call at 18:23:25 (F13) preceded the cancellation, so NS-1(iii) is met; the rider's case does not rest on a failure of contact but on the driver ending the wait himself at 18:27:55 (F11).

Contested as to NS-1(ii): the only wait shown by the record is 6 min 0 s from the platform's recorded arrival at 18:21:55 to cancellation at 18:27:55 (F6, F4), and NS-1 counts the free wait from the later of the scheduled pickup time and arrival — with no scheduled pickup time in the record the 5-minute margin is proved only against arrival, so the driver cut the wait at the first moment it expired while the rider, by his own account, was one minute behind; DISP-002's 8-minute threshold applied from arrival would not have expired.

Partly contested: the timeline (F2, F5, F13, F4) does show over six minutes un-replied-to, but it equally shows the driver's last message gave his own reason — "I need to go already" (F11) — and no record of the rider's movements (F12 contains only the driver's messages, both timestamped), so the system records confirm the wait but not that the rider was a no-show rather than one minute away as she states.

Agreed, and the rider does not seek any flag or credit: both profiles show 0 upheld disputes in 90 days (F18, F19), so the profile facts decide nothing and the only live question is the $5.00 fee under NS-1/NS-3 (F8), a fixed amount the system rules on finally under TH-2.

Conceded on the substance: NS-1(i) and (iv) are met on the system records — arrival tapped at 18:21:55, 40 m from pickup (F7), stationary at the pickup 18:21:55–18:27:55 with no GPS gap (F3) — but that does not narrow the case to the wait alone; NS-1(iii) is also met (F5).

The wait is counted from the later of scheduled pickup time and arrival, and the only arrival in the record is the platform-recorded 18:21:55 with the "I'm Here" tap 40 m out (F6, F7); cancellation came 6 min 0 s later, past the 5-minute free wait, and the rider cites no scheduled pickup time from the table to displace that start (F4).

Agreed that NS-1(iii) is satisfied, and note the record shows not one but 2 in-app messages (18:22:25 and 18:27) plus 1 unanswered in-app call (18:23:25), which is more contact than the clause requires (F5, F10, F11, F13).

"No reply from you" is the stated reason in that same message, and the driver's statement says "No rider, so I cancelled" after waiting more than 5 minutes (F11, F14); nothing in his words names car trouble, a personal matter, another job or a refusal, and the app reason was left unpicked (F4), so the record reads as a rider no-show (NS-0 met), not NS-3.

The rider's account that he came out a minute after cancellation rests on his statement alone: the system records show the driver inside 200 m from 18:21:40 and unanswered messages at 18:22:25 and 18:27 plus an unanswered call at 18:23:25 before cancelling at 18:27:55 (F2, F4, F5, F13), and the $5.00 was charged at the correct NS-1/NS-2 rate (F8).

Agreed the profiles decide nothing, and they do not cut the rider's way: the rider has 0 disputes and 0 no-shows in 90 days (F18) and the driver has 488 trips in 90 days with 0 upheld disputes (F19), so NS-9 and RD-6 are not triggered and no flag_account is added.
